why_trail.why: Rework of a BLOCKed prose gate: the five original doc edits stand and are confirmed; the one defect is that docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md still calls the gauge record four fields while g2 (5491bd4) shipped an optional fifth, identity_resolution_ms, on the dispatched-agent path only. Scope now also allows comment-only edits in scripts/hooks/gauge_writer_hook.py. The decisive risk is under-enumeration - the handoff named one doc site, the reviewer found two, so every site must be found by command across the doc and both hook files, with the count stated.

Enumerated by command, not from the anchor list: 13 matching lines across the doc and both hook files; SIX distinct sites assert the four-field/frozen-record claim (doc 35, doc 164, doc 251's frozen epithet, hook 20, hook 353, hook 403-404) and seven hits are a different claim (installer four-state report, skip-cause arithmetic, the two frozen DESIGN_SPEC references, and g2's two already-correct required-field comments). The reviewer found two sites; the real count is six.

All three doc sites corrected plus the JSON sample qualified: line 35 now names the four required fields and the optional fifth; a new short section 'The record is four required fields, plus one on a subagent' is the single authoritative statement (table, what identity_resolution_ms measures, the 100ms budget asserted at tests/test_gauge_writer.py:1201, and why a top-level record is unchanged); the eyeball check now tells a human five fields on a subagent's gauge is correct; the field table's 'frozen record' epithet is dropped. The two cosmetic over-wide lines the reviewer named in my own prior diff are rewrapped.

Three comment sites in gauge_writer_hook.py corrected: the module docstring now says four REQUIRED fields plus one optional fifth on the dispatched-agent path; compute_record's docstring says four is what that function returns and names the caller that adds the fifth; the sidecar comment no longer calls the record frozen at four and distinguishes an uncalibrated no-reading from an additive field on a real reading. The reviewer's second comment candidate (find_latest_usage's 'the field table is wrong about this today') is a DIFFERENT claim - sidechain polarity, not field count - so it stays, per the handoff. Comments-only proven mechanically by AST equality against HEAD with docstrings stripped, and the guard was shown red against a one-line mutation.

Post-edit enumeration re-run after the last edit (20 hits, false-assertion grep exits 1), sidechain sweep re-archived at live line numbers (5 lines / 7 occurrences), diff limited to the document plus comment lines with AST equality proving the code identical to HEAD, and the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT rewritten to cover the rework while keeping the original five edits' evidence. Suite run by the engine to pin the count.
